scope: The `checks` prompt arm for next-prompt (Tab) guesses: the history it came from, an offline replay against the current prompt, the live log baseline, and the live split that decides it. Model behavior and evaluator only; no GUI, attention-protocol, long-run or 32-session qualification.

history_basis.source: The operator's Claude Code transcripts on all their machines, 2026-09-22 to 2026-10-26, typed prompts only; corrections tagged by a separate model (obvious, taste or missing context).
history_basis.prompt_length_and_constraints: No effect on redo at any prompt length; more stated constraints went with more redo (odds 1.38x at 2, 1.56x at 3+, June to October), read as task difficulty.

live_log_baseline_redo.method: scripts/next_prompt_eval.py log --redo on the live log before this change (2026-09-30 to 2026-10-26): the person's next message after the agent answered each settled prompt, regex-classified.
live_log_baseline_redo.note: Taken guesses are followed by more continue and status messages than the person's own prompts; pushback alone is close (8 of 170 against 23 of 654). Taken and own prompts are not randomized, so this is a baseline, not an effect.

replay.method: 60 prompts sampled from local Claude Code and Codex transcripts since 2026-10-01 (seed 26), saved as one manifest and run under each prompt arm with the base context arm and the configured provider chain (a private DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 deployment first, a hosted fallback second). One Opus 5.5 judge call per eight items graded each arm's three candidates blind with the existing 0/1/2 rubric.
replay.reading: The checks shortened guesses (median 11 to 7 words) without raising sendable guesses (top-1 8 to 6 of 60, top-3 11 to 7) and produced no correction guesses (2 to 0). At 60 prompts these differences are within noise. Most sampled replies predate the 2026-10-20 instruction that agents restate the goal first, so the misread check had little to compare offline.

live_decision.split: promptArms base and checks, half and half, drawn apart from the context arm and logged as prompt_arm.
live_decision.rule: Keep checks if, at about 200 seen guesses per arm, its acceptance is higher and the redo rate after its taken guesses is not higher; otherwise set promptArms to ["base"].
live_decision.power: A 7-point acceptance gap (8% against 15%) is about 2.2 standard errors at 200 seen guesses per arm; at recent volumes that is roughly two weeks.

limitations: The replay grades against what was typed, so a shorter guess with the right intent but missing specifics scores 1, not 2; acceptance and redo are measured live only.
The judge labels each actual message's category per run, so category counts differ slightly between the two arms.
Redo is a regex on the start of the next message; interrupts and corrections phrased without the listed cues are missed.
Replay rows did not record which provider answered each guess; `answered_by` was added to the replay report after these runs.
